name: Radish
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 42 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days. Mississippi State University Extension gives a volume example of 2 to 3 tablespoons of radish seed per 10 by 20 inch tray, which is a different way of measuring the same job.

name: Pea
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: About 6 hours (Utah State). Maryland also lists 6 to 12 hours.
timing: Cover about 3 days. Harvest about 8 to 10 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 150 g per 1020 tray.
note: Utah State presoaks pea seed about 6 hours. University of Maryland Extension lists pea among seeds often soaked 6 to 12 hours. Covered about 3 days. Harvest about 8 to 10 days.

name: Sunflower
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
timing: Cover about 3 days. Harvest about 9 to 10 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 48 g per 1020 tray.
note: Utah State presoaks sunflower about 12 hours. Covered about 3 days. Harvest about 9 to 10 days. Penn State Extension recommends weight on sunflower seed during germination so hulls release from the cotyledons.

name: Broccoli
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 2 to 4 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 28 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 2 to 4 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.

name: Kale
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 28 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.

name: Arugula
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 6 to 8 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 10 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 6 to 8 days.

name: Cilantro
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: Utah State: no. Maryland: 6 to 12 hours may help.
timing: Cover 7 to 14 days. Harvest about 21 to 28 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 28 g per 1020 tray.
note: Utah State lists no presoak. University of Maryland Extension includes cilantro among seeds that may be soaked 6 to 12 hours. Covered about 7 to 14 days. Harvest about 21 to 28 days.

name: Basil
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 4 to 7 days. Harvest about 12 to 16 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 28 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 4 to 7 days. Harvest about 12 to 16 days.

name: Rutabaga
kind: Utah State crop rate for a 1020 tray
presoak: No presoak in the Utah State table
timing: Cover 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.
source: Utah State University Extension, 28 g per 1020 tray.
note: No presoak in the Utah State table. Covered about 1 to 2 days. Harvest about 8 to 12 days.

name: Mustard
presoak: Not specified as a mustard-only step
timing: Mississippi State groups mustard at about 10 to 15 days.
source: No crop-specific gram rate was published in the Utah State table. This band is the University of Maryland Extension sample broadcast of about 10 to 15 g (about 1 tablespoon) per 10 by 20 inch flat. It is not a mustard-only weighed rate.
note: Mustard is a small brassica seed. Mississippi State University Extension groups mustard with crops often ready about 10 to 15 days after sowing. Treat 10 to 15 g as a starting band for a nominal 10 by 20 inch flat, then adjust the next tray.

name: Beet
presoak: Maryland lists beet among seeds soaked 6 to 12 hours.
timing: Illinois: slower to germinate. Mississippi State: about 16 to 25 days.
source: No crop-specific gram rate was published in the Utah State table. This band is the University of Maryland Extension sample broadcast of about 10 to 15 g per 10 by 20 inch flat. Beet is listed in that publication's seed-count examples, not as its own weighed tray rate.
note: University of Maryland Extension lists beet among seeds that may be soaked 6 to 12 hours. Illinois Extension groups beet with slower-to-germinate choices. Mississippi State University Extension groups beets at about 16 to 25 days.

name: Amaranth
presoak: Illinois suggests a 6 to 24 hour soak can speed slower seeds.
timing: Illinois: slower to germinate. Mississippi State: red amaranth about 16 to 25 days.
source: No crop-specific gram rate was published in the Utah State table. This band is the University of Maryland Extension sample broadcast of about 10 to 15 g per 10 by 20 inch flat. Amaranth is named as a suitable crop there, not given its own gram rate.
note: Illinois Extension groups amaranth with slower-to-germinate choices. Mississippi State University Extension groups red amaranth at about 16 to 25 days. The 10 to 15 g band is a general small-seed starting point, not an amaranth trial result.
